source: CEEW draft indicator list for the VRA (all sheets), with direction and placement fixes from docs/vra-integration-plan.md

indicators.name: Heatwave days in the latest 12 complete months
indicators.rationale: Computed by CHART from ERA5: sum of monthly heatwave days over the latest 12 complete months held for the area. Stands in for CEEW's hot-day indices until the percentile-based indices are pulled.

value_schema.expected_values: a whole number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Mean of monthly peak maximum temperature, latest 12 complete months
indicators.rationale: Computed by CHART from ERA5: mean of each month's hottest daily maximum over the latest 12 complete months. Higher peak temperatures mean greater heat stress.

indicators.name: Number of flood events
indicators.rationale: Flooding can cripple health systems by inundating, damaging healthcare facilities, spreading waterborne diseases, and disrupting access to care.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Flood-inundated area, highest annual event 2020–2024
indicators.rationale: Captures the spatial extent of flooding. Dropped: CEEW suggests skipping it because a district is too coarse; flooding is concentrated in a few blocks.

indicators.name: Meteorological drought events
indicators.rationale: Drought-induced water scarcity may force populations to rely on unsafe or lower-quality water sources and constrain water for sanitation and hygiene.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Cyclone events
indicators.rationale: Not applicable to inland areas such as Madhya Pradesh; kept in the catalogue so coastal frames can enable it.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Change in extreme hot days, 2015–2024 vs 1982–2011
indicators.rationale: Rising temperatures can intensify the hydrological cycle and alter the transmission and seasonality of climate-sensitive diseases, including diarrhoeal diseases, malaria, dengue and cholera, with children being particularly vulnerable to these impacts.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Change in very hot days, 2015–2024 vs 1982–2011
indicators.rationale: Rising temperatures can intensify the hydrological cycle and alter the transmission and seasonality of climate-sensitive diseases, including diarrhoeal diseases, malaria, dengue and cholera, with children being particularly vulnerable to these impacts.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Warm nights (Tmin > 90th percentile) vs 1982–2011
indicators.rationale: Warm nights indicate persistently elevated nighttime temperatures that prevent physiological recovery from daytime heat exposure, raising the risk of heat-related illness, cardiovascular and respiratory mortality.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Extreme warm nights (Tmin > 95th percentile) vs 1982–2011
indicators.rationale: Warm nights indicate persistently elevated nighttime temperatures that prevent physiological recovery from daytime heat exposure, raising the risk of heat-related illness, cardiovascular and respiratory mortality.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Days with daily maximum heat index ≥ 39.4 °C, 2015–2024
indicators.rationale: The Heat Index combines air temperature and relative humidity to estimate the apparent temperature experienced by the human body; high values indicate greater physiological heat stress.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Projected change in extreme hot days, 2026–2045 (SSP2-4.5)
indicators.rationale: Projected trends in extreme events indicate how hazard intensity and frequency are likely to change under future climate scenarios, supporting anticipatory planning of health and WASH services.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Projected change in very warm nights, 2026–2045 (SSP2-4.5)
indicators.rationale: Projected trends in extreme events indicate how hazard intensity and frequency are likely to change under future climate scenarios, supporting anticipatory planning of health and WASH services.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Extremely heavy rainfall days (≥ 204.5 mm)
indicators.rationale: Heavy rainfall raises the likelihood of flooding and waterlogging, can damage health and WASH infrastructure, contaminate water sources and increase water-borne and vector-borne disease risk.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Very heavy rainfall days (≥ 115.6 mm)
indicators.rationale: Heavy rainfall raises the likelihood of flooding and waterlogging, can damage health and WASH infrastructure, contaminate water sources and increase water-borne and vector-borne disease risk.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Maximum 24-hour rainfall, 2020–2024
indicators.rationale: The highest short-duration rainfall intensity in the area, indicating potential for flash floods, urban flooding and infrastructure damage that disrupt healthcare delivery.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Projected change in heavy rainfall days, 2026–2045 (SSP2-4.5)
indicators.rationale: Projected changes in heavy rainfall days indicate shifts in rainfall-related hazards, including flooding and disruptions to healthcare infrastructure.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Heat-stress days (UTCI > 32 °C)
indicators.rationale: For human-health thresholds, days of exceedance of a thermal comfort index such as UTCI are more relevant than air temperature alone.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Population density
indicators.rationale: High population density accelerates the spread of infectious diseases, strains healthcare resources and increases exposure to environmental health risks.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Workers (main and marginal)
indicators.rationale: Labourers working outdoors and indoors face direct exposure to extreme weather such as heatwaves, heavy rains and cold spells. Expressed as a share so it does not measure district size.

indicators.name: Cultivators and agricultural labourers
indicators.rationale: Agricultural and allied workers face direct, prolonged outdoor exposure to heat, extreme weather and vector-borne disease, and their livelihoods are highly climate-sensitive.

indicators.name: Construction workers
indicators.rationale: Construction workers face prolonged outdoor heat exposure with limited workplace protections, making them a priority occupational group for heat-health interventions.

indicators.name: Veterinary hospitals, clinics and dispensaries
indicators.rationale: Dropped: CEEW notes it need not be considered.

value_schema.expected_values: a whole number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Children aged 0–6
indicators.rationale: Young children are physiologically more susceptible to heat stress, dehydration, respiratory and water-borne illness, and depend on caregivers and health services.

indicators.name: Population aged 65 and over
indicators.rationale: Older adults have lower thermoregulatory capacity and weaker immune systems, making them more susceptible to climate-sensitive health impacts.

indicators.name: Slum population
indicators.rationale: Informal settlements typically have poorer housing quality, drainage and basic services, heightening sensitivity to heat, flooding and disease outbreaks.

indicators.name: Women aged 20–49
indicators.rationale: Women are disproportionately affected by climate-related health risks, particularly for maternal and reproductive health. Expressed as a share so it does not measure district size.

indicators.name: Adolescent girls aged 15–19
indicators.rationale: Adolescent girls are particularly vulnerable to climate-related disruptions affecting nutrition, menstrual hygiene, education, reproductive health and psychosocial well-being.

indicators.name: Persons with disability
indicators.rationale: Persons with disabilities often have specialised needs for mobility and may find it harder to evacuate or reach safe areas during floods and heatwaves.

indicators.name: Women with high or very high blood sugar
indicators.rationale: Diabetes and uncontrolled blood sugar increase susceptibility to heat-related illness, cardiovascular complications, infections, and mortality during extreme weather events.

indicators.name: Men with high or very high blood sugar
indicators.rationale: Diabetes and uncontrolled blood sugar increase susceptibility to heat-related illness, cardiovascular complications, infections, and mortality during extreme weather events.

indicators.name: Women with elevated blood pressure
indicators.rationale: Hypertension increases the risk of cardiovascular events, particularly during heatwaves and other climate-related stressors.

indicators.name: Men with elevated blood pressure
indicators.rationale: Hypertension increases the risk of cardiovascular events, particularly during heatwaves and other climate-related stressors.

indicators.name: Anaemic women aged 15–49
indicators.rationale: Anaemia reduces physical capacity and immune function, increasing vulnerability to heat stress, infectious diseases, pregnancy-related complications and other climate-sensitive outcomes.

indicators.name: Children under 5 who are stunted
indicators.rationale: Malnutrition weakens immune function and increases susceptibility to infectious diseases, heat stress and food insecurity; districts with a higher prevalence of child malnutrition are more sensitive to climate-related health impacts.

indicators.name: Children under 5 who are wasted
indicators.rationale: Malnutrition weakens immune function and increases susceptibility to infectious diseases, heat stress and food insecurity; districts with a higher prevalence of child malnutrition are more sensitive to climate-related health impacts.

indicators.name: Children under 5 who are underweight
indicators.rationale: Malnutrition weakens immune function and increases susceptibility to infectious diseases, heat stress and food insecurity; districts with a higher prevalence of child malnutrition are more sensitive to climate-related health impacts.

indicators.name: Children under 5 who are overweight
indicators.rationale: Malnutrition weakens immune function and increases susceptibility to infectious diseases, heat stress and food insecurity; districts with a higher prevalence of child malnutrition are more sensitive to climate-related health impacts.

indicators.name: Infant mortality rate
indicators.rationale: Infants are physiologically more susceptible to heat stress, dehydration, diarrhoeal diseases and respiratory infections; a high infant mortality rate reflects underlying health, nutrition and WASH vulnerabilities.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Stage of groundwater extraction
indicators.rationale: Groundwater is a major source of water for WASH services; extraction beyond safe limits threatens the quantity and quality of water available.

value_schema.expected_values: a non-negative percentage; values above 100 are allowed

indicators.name: Flood susceptibility
indicators.rationale: Areas highly susceptible to flooding are more likely to experience inundation of homes, health facilities and WASH infrastructure. CEEW 30 m landscape susceptibility analysis, reduced to the share of the area in the high or very high class.

indicators.name: Heat susceptibility
indicators.rationale: Landscapes with limited vegetation and dense built-up area experience higher local temperatures, raising heat stress and water demand. CEEW 30 m landscape susceptibility analysis, reduced to the share of the area in the high or very high class.

indicators.name: Drought susceptibility
indicators.rationale: Drought-prone landscapes face recurrent water scarcity, increasing sensitivity to water-borne diseases, malnutrition and livelihood loss. CEEW 30 m landscape susceptibility analysis, reduced to the share of the area in the high or very high class.

indicators.name: Flood susceptibility of roads
indicators.unit: % of road length in high class
indicators.rationale: Roads susceptible to flooding are likely to be cut off during heavy rainfall, limiting access to healthcare, evacuation routes and essential supplies.

indicators.name: Change in forest cover
indicators.rationale: Forests regulate local temperature, moderate runoff and support water recharge; loss of forest cover heightens sensitivity to heat, flooding and water quality degradation. A gain lowers risk.

value_schema.expected_values: a signed number (negative, zero or positive)

indicators.name: Green space per person
indicators.rationale: Green spaces reduce urban heat, improve air quality and support drainage; a higher value indicates lower sensitivity.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Malaria annual parasite incidence
indicators.rationale: Directly climate-sensitive (temperature and rainfall driven). Filed under adaptive capacity in the draft sheet; it is a sensitivity. District data is held by programme officers.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: HIV prevalence
indicators.rationale: Dropped: CEEW's own comment; 2019 district data is banded and has low relevance to heat.

indicators.name: Cyclone susceptibility
indicators.rationale: Not applicable to inland areas such as Madhya Pradesh; kept in the catalogue so coastal frames can enable it.

indicators.name: Women aged 15–49 with 10 or more years of schooling
indicators.rationale: Education improves health literacy, awareness of climate-related health risks, uptake of preventive measures, and ability to access and interpret early warning information. Educated women also contribute to better household preparedness and health-seeking behaviour.

indicators.name: Men aged 15–49 with 10 or more years of schooling
indicators.rationale: Education improves health literacy, awareness of climate-related health risks, uptake of preventive measures, and ability to access and interpret early warning information.

indicators.name: Children 12–23 months fully vaccinated
indicators.rationale: High vaccination coverage reflects strong primary healthcare and reduces susceptibility to infectious diseases that may increase after floods and extreme rainfall.

indicators.name: Households with any member covered by health insurance or a financing scheme
indicators.rationale: Health insurance reduces financial barriers to healthcare, enabling timely treatment during climate-related illnesses and emergencies.

indicators.name: Average out-of-pocket expenditure per delivery in a public facility
indicators.rationale: High out-of-pocket expenditure can discourage timely healthcare seeking and increase financial hardship during climate-related health emergencies.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Households with an improved drinking-water source
indicators.rationale: Reliable access to safe drinking water reduces vulnerability to water-borne diseases and enhances resilience during droughts, floods and heatwaves.

indicators.name: Households using an improved sanitation facility
indicators.rationale: Improved sanitation reduces exposure to water-borne and faecal-oral diseases, particularly during flooding and heavy rainfall events.

indicators.name: Households using clean fuel for cooking
indicators.rationale: Clean cooking fuel reflects household living standards (a component of India's multidimensional poverty index) and reduces indoor air pollution exposure.

indicators.name: Households owning a vehicle
indicators.rationale: Ownership of private transport reflects household economic capacity and mobility, enabling faster evacuation and access to healthcare after climate-related disasters.

indicators.name: Rural households with destitutes or living on alms
indicators.rationale: Indicates extreme poverty: households with almost no economic buffer to cope with or recover from a hazard.

indicators.name: Households with phone, internet or television
indicators.rationale: Access to mobile and wireline technology enables receipt of early warnings and health advisories and communication with health services during climate-related events.

indicators.name: Public health facilities per 100,000 population
indicators.rationale: The higher the number of functional health facilities, the greater the preparedness to respond to health concerns during a disaster. Moved from exposure to adaptive capacity, as its own rationale implies.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Health workforce gap (sanctioned posts vacant)
indicators.rationale: Adequately staffed facilities determine the capacity to respond to increased demand during extreme weather and outbreaks; a larger gap means less capacity.

indicators.name: Rural schools and anganwadis with tap drinking water
indicators.rationale: Safe water in schools and anganwadis supports child health, hygiene and continuity of essential services during climate extremes.

indicators.name: Rural schools and anganwadis with running water in toilets
indicators.rationale: Safe water in schools and anganwadis supports child health, hygiene and continuity of essential services during climate extremes.

indicators.name: Heat-related illness and mortality surveillance in place
indicators.rationale: Surveillance of heat-related illness and mortality enables timely detection and public health action, strengthening capacity to respond to heat.

indicators.name: Heat action plan exists
indicators.rationale: Heat action plans provide a framework for early warning, awareness, coordination and healthcare preparedness, reducing heat-related morbidity and mortality.

indicators.name: Road network density
indicators.rationale: A dense road network improves connectivity to healthcare, enables faster evacuation and emergency response, and supports recovery after climate-related events.

value_schema.expected_values: a number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Multidimensionally poor population (NITI Aayog MPI)
indicators.rationale: India's national MPI covers health, education and standard of living across 12 indicators; higher deprivation means less capacity to cope.

indicators.name: District Mental Health Programme coverage
indicators.rationale: Strengthens access to decentralised mental healthcare after climate-related disasters. State-level, so shown as context rather than scored.

indicators.name: State health adaptation plan components (SAPCCHH)
indicators.rationale: Sector-specific health adaptation plans reflect institutional preparedness. State-level, so shown as context rather than scored.

value_schema.expected_values: a whole number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Sentinel surveillance hospitals for dengue and chikungunya
indicators.rationale: Dropped: only a handful per state, so no spread between districts.

value_schema.expected_values: a whole number greater than or equal to 0

indicators.name: Functional One Health / zoonotic surveillance units
indicators.rationale: Dropped: CEEW notes it can be removed.

value_schema.expected_values: a whole number greater than or equal to 0
